table.description:
Knock-detection background step for event slot 3, frequency channel 8. It has no effect on a stock car because this channel is switched off in the knock processing calibration (channels 1, 7 and 8 are disabled). Stock 0 everywhere.
Details: Unused in stock: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 3 (Event 3), knock channel 8 of 8 (index 7 of FFF8CDB0), which is masked: bit 7 of cal 0x1B97E is set (0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off for every slot). 0x0E51E4 (read) then writes a fixed ratio for the channel instead of 256 x measured/reference, and the reference ref_7 (the only place this step enters, statics FFF84AB4..FFF84AD0 read only by 0x0E51E4, ram_xref) is not used; the reference copies FFF8C130.. have no reader. So editing it has no effect unless that cal bit is cleared, which would make the channel count (then this would be the background step for FFF8C1A0[7] when FFF8A7C4 changes; overlap flag FFF8A7D4, gain curve cal 0x26F8F). Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Stock 0 everywhere. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06AF58, read). ADC channel 19 (0xFFFFE864, untrimmed) -> FFF88D38 -> FFF88F30, filtered by cal 0x579B6 (65535 = no filter in stock) -> FFF88F34 / FFF88F32, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) to give FFF88662 = degC + 50: the OBD IAT FFF8CEE5, the IAT behind FFF88A48 (the IAT axis of the timing, boost, throttle and fuel compensation tables) and the IAT read by fuel 0x0C589C and purge 0x0D4E78 (for Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro), 0x0D44DC) (read). This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V (identical to IAT 2). Descriptor boot 0539D4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06B304, read). ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 (no filter in stock) -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. Probably the thermistor of the manifold TMAP sensor (inferred from its use as the manifold air temperature): when fitting a different TMAP / MAP sensor with its own thermistor, change these temperature values. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock identical to IAT 1. Descriptor boot 0539E0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). Coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (input 0 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed, 65536 = 5 V inferred) is filtered by cal 0x56EE8 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88ADC and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC) into FFF88AE8 / FFF88AE0 (256 x (degC + 50)): FFF8CD65 (coolant byte, degC + 50), the OBD coolant value and FFF88A44 (the coolant axis of most tables). While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) a warm-up model from cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2 replaces it. Range faults: P0117 below Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0118 above Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25.7 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V. Change only when fitting a different sensor. Descriptor boot 0539F8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BEA0, read). Oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (input 7 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed) is filtered by cal 0x56F76 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88AE4 and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC). Output unit 256 x (degC + 50), read: FFF88E24 = (output - 0xA00) x 256 / 205 and OBD PID 0x5C reports FFF88E24 x 205 / 65536 = degC + 40. FFF88E24 / FFF88E26 is the oil temperature of the AVCS and idle tables (oil_temp_obd axis). Range faults: P0197 below Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0198 above Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock identical to the coolant curve. Descriptor boot 053A04. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description:
Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling. Identical to A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich) in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while FFF88AFB bit 4 is clear: the A/F signal is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37 (window -800..1000 with hysteresis 333, 0x0843F8, read); gain cal 0x571F0 = 2. Identical to Near Stoich in stock; edit both together. 0x06C1A8 (read): the A/F sensor signal FFF88B2E is looked up here (boot lookup 0x6A0C) into FFF88AF6, the measured lambda of the closed loop (B308 = 43194 x 32768 / FFF88AF6, 0x0FF3CC). Stock lambda 1.00 at signal -25...0. Descriptor boot 053A10. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description:
Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain. Shares its axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range) and is identical to it in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while the A/F signal is within about lambda 0.90-1.37 (FFF88AFB bit 4 set, 0x0843F8, read); higher gain cal 0x571F1 = 9 (gain reading inferred). Second A/F sensor table in 0x06C1A8 (read); shares the axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range). Identical to it in stock; edit both together. Descriptor boot 053A1C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool. Stock: full at the lowest input, empty at the highest.
Details: When used: always (0x06C336, read). Input: the fuel sender reading sent by the combination meter on CAN 0x282 bytes 0-1 (10-bit, FFF88E04 -> 0x1108B8 -> FFF8B43C; not an ECU analog input). 0x06C336 forms FFF88BD0 = FFF8B43C x 2867 / (FFF8B43C + cal 0x572E0 (720)), filters it into FFF88BCC and looks it up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF88BD4; FFF88BD7 is its average over cal 0x572E6 samples taken while FFF88A76 is at least cal 0x572E4, kept in backup RAM FFF806BB/806BC, and reported by OBD PID 0x2F as x 255 / 219 (read). So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Stock: full (219) at the lowest input, empty at 2432 and above. Descriptor boot 053A28. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Rail pressure floor by rpm for P0087 (rail pressure too low): the code counts a fault when actual pressure stays more than 0.30 MPa (hysteresis cal) below this value for about 10 seconds, i.e. below 0.40 MPa in stock, and recovers when pressure is back at this value. Stock 0.70 MPa at all rpm.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read, boot lookup 0x72AC): the absolute low-pressure test fails while actual rail pressure FFF88884 < this(rpm FFF8CD56) - hysteresis cal 0x574DA for cal 0x574E0 passes -> P0087. Stock 1148 = 0.70 MPa flat. p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Descriptor boot 053B3C. Confidence: read.
